transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Aisha (Celestia Head of Data), Rob (CTO), Nina (Security), Marcus (Infra), Priya (PM)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i can see we got a full house from celestia, quick round robin?
[00:10] Aisha: hi all, aisha here, head of data, i'll own the integration side and success metrics
[00:18] Rob: rob, cto - i'll be the exec sponsor and help unblock infra/security
[00:24] Nina: nina, security lead - focused on compliance, encryption and audits
[00:30] Marcus: marcus infra - i'll do the networking bits and internal access
[00:35] Priya: priya, product - i'll run acceptance criteria for the pilot
[00:40] Jordan: cool thanks. quick agenda: intros, success criteria/timeline, technical overview (maya), security/ops (liam + nina), next steps. feel free to interrupt.

[02:05] Maya: i'll start with a 10 minute high-level on how the onboarding typically works - hosted vs dedicated vs private. we recommend starting with hosted to iterate quickly then move to dedicated or private depending on data residency and throughput.
[02:20] Aisha: we have PHI-ish notes in some records; leaning toward private or dedicated. can you summarize differences?
[02:32] Maya: yeah. hosted is fastest - redwood-managed control plane, logs retained per tenant. dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and isolation, predictable throughput, better for steady high throughput. private (vpc/on-prem) gives you a private control plane, kms/hsm integrations and audit log export - common for regulated customers. there are tradeoffs: private takes longer to provision and needs network peering or on-prem install.
[03:10] Rob: timeline — how long to get private up and running?
[03:20] Maya: typical private deployment is 4-8 weeks depending on networking and approvals; if you start with hosted we can get you ingesting in days.

[04:00] Liam: from a cs angle, we usually propose a 6-week pilot: week1-2 access and basic test prompts, week3 run benchmark with your prompt set, week4 validate quality/regression, week5 optimizations (batching/quant), week6 handoff.
[04:18] Priya: that aligns with our roadmap. success metric for pilot is latency p95 < 400ms for the 99-token prompts and cost per 1k tokens under target. also quality measured on a 20-prompt eval set.

[05:12] Nina: on security, we need SOC 2 cert details, where logs live, and whether we can bring our own KMS. also SSO/SAML and RBAC.
[05:30] Jordan: yeah we'll send the security pack after this call; we support BYOK via KMS integration for private and dedicated. redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO-27001 docs in the security pack.
[05:50] Maya: for audit logs in private, you can export event logs to your splunk or s3; hosted has retention tiers we can configure.

[07:05] Marcus: network flow -- is the private control plane outbound only? we prefer no inbound tunnels.
[07:15] Maya: private control plane is customer-managed networking; we support peering and outbound initiation. for on-prem we ship an installer that establishes an outbound connection to the control plane but the model runtime stays inside your VPC. we can confirm exact ports.

[08:20] Aisha: data retention - we need confirmation that training data isn't retained or used for model training.
[08:30] Jordan: correct, we have contractual language and technical controls. hosted doesn't train on customer data; you can opt out and we can disable retention. private keeps everything in your environment. we will include the language in the security pack.

[09:45] Maya: technical checklist for pilot: sample prompts, prompt set for eval, SSO metadata, test accounts, network allowlist, sample payload sizes. also we need a short benchmark harness from your team - we can provide one.
[10:00] Priya: we'll assemble prompts and pass to aisha's team.

[12:10] Jordan: ok let's walk through the immediate next steps - i'll capture these. first: send onboarding playbook + security pack. second: schedule se deep dive for VPC/private options. third: celestia to provide sso metadata and test accounts. fourth: grant infra access for IP allowlist.

[13:25] Rob: about pricing - can you provide a rough estimate for a 6-week pilot and ballpark numbers for dedicated capacity?
[13:35] Jordan: i'll send a pilot pricing sheet. pilot usage in hosted is usage-based; dedicated has a monthly commit - i'll include a few tier options and typical performance profiles per model.

[15:00] Maya: on performance - we usually recommend smaller quantized variants for cost but we can run a benchmark on your prompt distribution to recommend quantization and batching settings. we'll instrument latency p50/p95 and token costs.
[15:20] Marcus: do we need special GPUs for private?
[15:28] Maya: depends on model - 8/16/24GB card choices. we'll propose hardware based on your throughput.

[18:00] Nina: regarding compliance, can you support audit log export frequency and retention windows? we need 7 years for certain entries.
[18:12] Liam: for private you control log retention; for hosted we have configurable tiers and enterprise add-ons for extended retention. we'll get exact SLA and retention options in the pack.

[21:00] Aisha: a quick question - for SSO, we need role mappings to align with our internal RBAC. can we map Okta groups to redwood roles?
[21:12] Maya: yes we support SAML and SCIM for provisioning; you can map groups to roles. we'll include an example mapping.

[24:30] Priya: pilot acceptance criteria recap - 1) quality on eval set within 5% of baseline, 2) latency p95 under target for specified prompt length, 3) security sign-off on SSO and KMS.
[24:50] Jordan: yep that's a good summary.

[27:10] Rob: any blockers you're seeing from other customers during private installs?
[27:20] Maya: mostly networking approvals and CISO sign-off timelines; we try to parallelize provisioning and security document review to keep things moving.

[30:00] Liam: ok i'll own the weekly check-ins and retrospective at the end of pilot. we'll assign an onboarding ticket in your repo and share a runbook.

[32:40] Jordan: i'll also create a shared folder with the playbook, pricing, security pack, and the benchmark harness. expect that by end of day tomorrow.

[35:10] Marcus: for the network allowlist, who will provide the exact IPs?
[35:20] Maya: i'll follow up with the infra IP ranges. for private we can also do peering so allowlist may not be needed.

[38:00] Nina: data residency question - can we pin runtime to region? we have EU data residency requirements for some clients.
[38:12] Maya: yes you can pin region for deployments; for private it's in your VPC region; for hosted we have region options and enterprise agreements for residency.

[41:30] Aisha: timeline - can we aim to start pilot on 2026-10-25? that's next monday.
[41:40] Jordan: tight but doable if we get SSO metadata and test accounts this week and we share the playbook tomorrow. we'll tentatively schedule start and adjust if provisioning slips.

[44:00] Priya: one last ask - can you share a sample of the benchmark harness and a short guide so our infra team can stand up load agents?
[44:10] Maya: yes we'll provide the harness and a docker-based agent; link in the playbook.

[46:15] Jordan: great, recap of next steps: jordan send playbook/security pack/pricing; maya schedule vpc deep dive + provide IP ranges and harness; nina provide sso metadata; marcus grant test access. set weekly cadence with liam. we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[46:40] Rob: thanks everyone, appreciated.
[46:45] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up. bye.
